problem: The table says a late deceleration 'starts after contraction peak'. Standard definition: a late deceleration begins after the contraction has started (in the latter part of the contraction), and its lowest point (nadir) comes after the peak of the contraction. A student who writes 'starts after the peak' loses marks.
fix: Late | begins after the contraction starts, nadir after the contraction peak | poor placental flow. (The worked example still holds: a fall that begins 20 s after the peak is a late deceleration.)

problem: Variability is written as '±5 beats per minute'. CTG variability is quoted as an amplitude in beats per minute (normally 5 to 25), not as a plus-minus band; ±5 suggests a 10 beats-per-minute swing.
fix: Write 'variability of 5 beats per minute (the lower end of the normal 5 to 25 range)'.

problem: The question asks for 'two quantities', but the answer gives one quantity (the RR interval in seconds) plus a formula. The second item is a relation, not a quantity.
fix: Ask: 'What measurement does an arrhythmia monitor take, and what relation converts it to rate?' Answer: the RR interval in seconds, converted by rate = 60/RR.

problem: The pause limit is drawn as a bar running from 0 to 1500 ms, which looks like a duration on the time axis rather than a threshold that the third interval crosses.
fix: Draw the pause limit as a vertical marker line at 1500 ms (or label it 'threshold 1500 ms'), so it is read as a level, not as a fourth interval.
